title: IV-VII: conditions of power — universality, immensity, perfection in work
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): it stands as not as already made, but as to-be-made, that same which stands as in ye power belonging toward ye maker plus not already made in act — and therefore by means belonging toward ye same power by means belonging toward that same which He could create ye world. Finally, to this power belonging toward God what stands as already done stands as not subject under ye reason belonging toward ye done, but under ye reason belonging toward being done. plus behold, they were very good — then God looked upon all things that same which He had made. Hence Moses in Genesis 1:31: Perfection in ye work stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God does most excellently whatever He does. VII. Immensity stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God by means belonging toward His power penetrates plus encompasses all things. VI. Universality stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God can do all things that same which He can will. V. universality, immensity, perfection in ye work. Its condition stands as threefold: IV.
pass_b_english: IV. Its condition is threefold: universality, immensity, perfection in the work. V. Universality is that by which God can do all things which He can will. VI. Immensity is that by which God by His power penetrates and encompasses all things. VII. Perfection in the work is that by which God does most excellently whatever He does. Hence Moses in Genesis 1:31: Then God looked upon all things which He had made, and behold, they were very good.

Finally, to this power of God what is already done is not subject under the reason of the done, but under the reason of being done. And therefore by the same power by which He could create the world, it is not as already made, but as to-be-made, which is in the power of the maker and not already made in act.
source_text: IV. Conditio ejus est triplex: universalitas, immensitas, perfectio in opere. V. Universalitas est, qua Deus omnia potest quae velle potest. VI. Immensitas est, qua Deus potentia sua omnia penetrat et ambit. VII. Perfectio in opere est, qua Deus optime facit quicquid facit. Hinc Moses Gen. I.31: Tum inspexisse Deum omnia quae fecerat, et ecce bona valde. Ad extremum huic potentiae Dei non subjicitur factum sub ratione facti, sed sub ratione fiendi. Et ideo eadem potentia qua potuit creare mundum, non factum, sed faciendum, quod in potentia facientis est et non in actu factus.
